bounded_lifecycle_feasibility.conclusion: The reviewed selected-plugin finalizer repair is independently useful product correctness. The retained startup evidence establishes no second random-value or guest-clock-value defect. Do not begin a broad bootstrap rewrite solely to change the red comparator result.
earliest_constraints: R loader premain.c:139-144 deliberately initializes the plugin in preinit after relocation/GOT availability. ld_sc_handler.c:250-277 requires loader TLS and explains why forwarding ARCH_SET_FS into allocator/pthread-using plugin code before client TLS initialization is unsafe. Moving the existing Rust connection earlier is not a supported fix.

R reverie_adapter.rs:438-462 connects RPC, constructs T, resolves inherited fork state, then constructs the normal root and applies its initializer. H ThreadState::new at tool_local.rs:2145 also discovers fd0..2 using current-process fcntl/fstat (688-724). Running that same constructor in the out-of-process supervisor would discover supervisor descriptors.

H handle_thread_start at detcore/src/lib.rs:1643-1716 performs real global registration, scheduling and clock hooks; handle_post_exec at1719 consumes the authenticated auxv fact. These callbacks cannot be synthesized at handoff or repeated without changing state. R Tool::init_thread_state documents creation before the first guest instruction (reverie/src/tool.rs:429-454).
minimal_dependency_sequence: For a genuine pre-interpreter shared-Tool path: R first needs a backward-compatible, explicitly negotiated early guest-interception/continuation boundary, preserving native loader-private operations and static/exec/fork legacy paths. A stopped external Guest or equivalent actual Tool execution provider must act on guest memory/injections and guest metadata; no backend-local reproduction of Detcore semantics. This is a core interception/lifecycle change, not a small loader guard.

After reviewed R delivery, H may advance its R pin monotonically and consume that boundary in sabre_bootstrap/sabre_ptrace plus detcore-sabre. Keep one live root Tool state through real bootstrap operations and authenticated transition. Existing global state/RPC must remain authoritative across both phases; merely serializing the current random capsule cannot close the routing gap.

The bounded RNG-only alternative is an additive R root-state factory after the existing fork decision, with current connect/initializer APIs unchanged, then H shared construction that adopts the authenticated already-advanced RNG exactly once while constructing unrelated state normally. Preserve static/exec continuation behavior, all identity checks and real event emission. It does not change the 25 native startup routes or establish parity, and current evidence supports lifecycle/evidence hardening rather than a guest-value correction.
bounded_lifecycle_feasibility.narrow_product_candidates: No additional independently proven guest-correctness repair follows from the first auxv/USER RAND mismatch. The reference rseq returns ENOSYS while source routes pre-plugin SaBRe rseq natively; robust-list/clear-child-tid registrations likewise bypass shared handlers. These are specific coverage risks, not observed candidate return values or permission to emulate them in a backend helper. They would require separately dispatched evidence before choosing a narrow fix.
bounded_lifecycle_feasibility.recommendation: Keep the finalizer fix ready for normal R-first delivery once account state changes. Park startup implementation until a separately scoped genuine guest correctness target is established; do not present RNG-constructor or collector cleanup as resolving the full startup parity failure.
bounded_lifecycle_feasibility.reusable_state_and_limit: Reuse shared Detcore handlers, the existing authenticated IMAGE/GETRANDOM/TAKE owner/config/image checks, and the real advanced Pcg64Mcg. Tool::ThreadState is already serializable and SaBRe has a same-tool process-fork codec, but that codec creates a child from parent state; it is not authority to resume the same root across execution providers. Full continuation must preserve clocks/counters, metadata/open-file identities, memory identity, scheduler registration, robust-list state, RNGs and record/replay state, with one owner and no reset/reseed/re-registration. Existing random handoff intentionally carries none of those non-random fields.
bounded_lifecycle_feasibility.scope: Read-only source/retained-evidence assessment; only this section appended. No source, ref, index, target, runtime or public action.
bounded_lifecycle_feasibility.separate_event_transport: Appending plugin records after process exit loses producer order independently of state handoff. A faithful shared emission-time transport could improve evidence, but cannot repair guest routing and must not sort, drop, retimestamp, synthesize events or relax comparison.
bounded_lifecycle_feasibility.trigger_assessment: A genuine early shared-Tool provider and same-root transition changes the syscall-interception/lifecycle model: post-facto trigger2 applies even if Tool trait signatures stay unchanged. Trigger4 additionally applies if core scheduling behavior changes. The narrower factory must be assessed against its final callback/construction contract; replacing the documented root initialization model also triggers2. Pure faithful event transport has no automatic core trigger. No new determinization algorithm is justified.

strict_cross_report.first_divergent_left_message: INFO detcore::tool_local: DETLOG USER RAND: seeding PRNG for root thread with seed 0
strict_cross_report.first_divergent_right_message: INFO detcore::random: DETLOG [post_exec, dtid 3] init auxv AT_RANDOM value to [162, 205, 24, 211, 0, 83, 122, 92, 176, 131, 220, 72, 219, 250, 14, 242]

findings: The exact first divergence is a different initialization event, not a differing time field or random payload. Both retained streams have identical sixteen AT_RANDOM bytes and identical first eight-byte getrandom hash 9401673912765844831.

SaBRe supervisor constructs the actual seeded PRNG before IMAGE, performs shared initialize_auxv and getrandom before plugin readiness, then hands its advanced state to a normally constructed root. The later normal constructor emits USER/CHAOS seed records for fresh initial state before the authenticated PRNG replacement; completed auxv identity prevents a second draw/write/event.

This establishes split initialization ownership and a misleading global event sequence, not an observed initial random-byte corruption. The collector separately appends plugin records only after child completion, losing global producer order; sorting those records would not establish shared lifecycle parity.

The retained ptrace trace has26 loader/bootstrap inbound syscall records before getpid; fixed SaBRe has only the six main-program inbound syscall records. This is a separate shared-tool startup coverage gap. Source classifies one getrandom through the shared random helper, ten calls through native loader substrate wrappers, and fifteen through native default forwarding; it does not prove exact one-for-one native SaBRe operands for the missing reference operations.

No common guest-visible clock_gettime return is recorded in pid-probe. Runtime logical-time totals differ, but that is not an observed mismatch in a guest clock read. Normal shared Detcore clock/scheduler/syscall accounting is absent from the early helper route.
